system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status note:** All Seller "agreed"/"settled"/"addressed"/"adequate" characterisations below are treated as assertions only (playbook 0.4/6.3). No Amelia Frost written authority is on file for any fallback.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl. 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure matches our fallback number but no Amelia Frost written authority identifying this draft exists, so it is not cleared — a coincidence of numbers is not approval.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl. 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar ("tipping") recovery once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject on all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the deductible structure would permanently forfeit the first AUD 250,000 of valid claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months; plus a sweep that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl. 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; limitations apply only to the category they name.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; hold at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is an unapproved fallback (no Amelia Frost sign-off), and the default-application language is a hidden override of the separate regimes (see N-014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime — 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright; this is a deal-critical point.** Capping title at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m share purchase means a title failure could leave us paying 100% for shares we do not own with 20% recourse.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5) — no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert express carve-out — non-negotiable, no one on our side may waive it.** Absent the carve-out the draft purports to limit the Seller's exposure for its own fraud, which is both unacceptable commercially and of doubtful enforceability.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 Sept 2026, Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records (Sch. 7; DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no whole-data-room, public-register or "prudent search" deeming.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DL 1.1–1.2 and the Schedule 7 mechanism; require a fair-disclosure standard.** Whole-data-room disclosure would convert every unindexed document into a warranty qualifier and effectively hollow out the warranty package.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl. 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion; any residual qualifier must reference named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl. 8.3 in full.** A "discoverable" standard plus adviser imputation is a constructive-knowledge bar that duplicates and compounds the N-006 problem and swallows the warranties.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl. 3/6.3). Seller "addressed" claim is contradicted by DL §2: **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** are in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring (a) effective, unconditional consent under cl. 11.2 AND (b) evidence that each cl. 11.3 condition is satisfied, both before Completion; Seller to use all reasonable/best endeavours; Buyer-only waiver right.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours; redraft as a two-limb CP.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m), and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms the matter is not in fact "addressed".

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl. 2/7). DL §3 confirms not repaid, no discharge documents.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow; executed security releases/discharges (incl. PPSR) delivered at Completion. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the post-completion release; require payout-at-Completion with releases in escrow.** Buying a debt-free/cash-free company while leaving AUD 3.2m of secured debt in place with no binding release defeats the price mechanics and leaves our asset encumbered.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL §5 confirms they are omitted and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals) either (i) a specific funds-flow line item paid from the Seller's proceeds, or (ii) treated as Debt/Transaction Expenses in the price adjustment, with a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insist on express line item or seller funding plus on-cost gross-up.** "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless once the Company — which we will own — is the legal employer and payer; silence in the funds flow means we fund it.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl. 11.1). DL §4: cl. 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but is not bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broadened indemnity covering (a) all amounts needed to perfect title to SOW3 Project Materials, (b) losses from any IP ownership/licence defect under the Ironquay arrangements, (c) third-party claims — while preserving the pre-Completion cure (pay the fee and deliver the confirmatory assignment). Independent verification of the AUD 180,000 (bank records / Ironquay statement) both ways.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "adequate"; broaden the indemnity and make the cure a Completion deliverable.** The real risk is non-vesting of Project Materials, not merely the unpaid invoice, and the AUD 180,000 figure is unverified in either direction.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** DD-006 is a "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material" (cl. 4.6/Sch. 6). DL §6: ~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined; investigation preliminary.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation, provide written updates and the final report; specific warranties as to the facts; a specific indemnity for losses, regulatory costs and notification costs if a breach/notifiable incident is established. Do **not** accept either the Seller's immateriality label or any assumption of a confirmed breach.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation; add investigation/update covenants and a contingent specific indemnity.** The record establishes neither breach nor harm nor a notification duty, so the right posture is evidence preservation and allocation of the unresolved risk to the Seller, not a numeric claim.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL §8 says the disclosure does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course — contradicting the Update's label.
- **Buyer wants:** Copies of the renewal terms, timing and termination rights; assessment of whether any amount is pre-Completion accrued liability or a non-ordinary commitment; confirmation they are reflected in the accounts/working capital. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label; request documents and assess before taking a position.** The Seller's own Disclosure Letter declines to characterise them, so we should neither concede nor demand a deduction until we have the facts.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl. 12.3/13 default (all limitations apply to all Claims unless stated); cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5 (limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"); Tax/IP folded into the general regime; Title folded into general caps.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate, self-contained regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, Completion payment obligations, specific indemnities and covenants; general limitations expressly stated **not** to apply to those categories unless specifically cross-referenced.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject all three sweep-up provisions and insert an express "regimes are independent" clause.** Collectively these are a structural override that would import the AUD 4.8m/18-month general limits into every other category through the back door.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of shares is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012. DL §10 concedes this is merely the source the Seller relies on and that Buyer verification is not completed.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence — ASIC company extract and historical extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, certificate of registration, constitution, share certificates/cancelled certificates, board and shareholder minutes evidencing allotments and transfers, confirmation no options/convertibles/pre-emptive rights, and a Seller authority/capacity opinion or resolutions. Title/capacity warranties unqualified by disclosure or knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not treat DD-012 as proof; run independent searches and make authority/encumbrance evidence Completion deliverables.** An internal register is a Seller-supplied document and cannot verify its own accuracy, particularly with a AUD 3.2m secured facility outstanding (Riverlark) that may extend to share security.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime above" (20% cap, 18 months, AUD 25k/250k thresholds).
- **Buyer wants:** Terms remain OPEN. Tax: separate regime (typically a tax indemnity/covenant with a cap at or near price and a period tied to the statutory review window, e.g. 7 years) — to be negotiated. IP: standalone warranties and the Ironquay indemnity (N-011) outside general limits — to be negotiated. We do not assume unlimited liability.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; record Tax and IP as expressly open in the issues list and the SPA.** Nothing has been agreed through our authority process, and the Seller's assertion of settlement is exactly the kind of statement the playbook directs us not to accept at face value.

---

## Summary of priority items for the response letter
1. **Deal-structure items (must-fix before any signing path):** N-004 Title regime, N-005 Fraud carve-out, N-008 Bluefen CP, N-009 Riverlark payout, N-014 category separation.
2. **Economic items (counter in full):** N-001 cap, N-002 thresholds, N-003 period, N-010 bonuses.
3. **Diligence/information requests to issue now:** N-011 Ironquay payment verification; N-012 incident log preservation and updates; N-013 Sandbar renewal terms; N-015 independent title/PPSR/ASIC searches.
4. **Hold open:** N-016 Tax/IP; no fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-completion Riverlark release) to be offered or accepted without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the specific draft.

**Observation for the team:** the Seller's Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Seller Update — on Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Sandbar and title it expressly concedes the matters are *not* resolved, directly contradicting the Update's "addressed/settled/adequate" labels. We should quote the Disclosure Letter back to the Seller on each of those points.
=== END ADVICE ===
